## My thinking as I plan this year

I've been at this 40 years, and on 6 mu you can't afford waste but you also can't afford to underfeed vegetables — cabbage especially is a heavy feeder and the fall crop pays for the whole year if I get the head weight right. My main rotation stays cabbage-maize-cabbage on about 4 mu of my better land. The other 2 mu I split: 1 mu chili near the house (my wife manages it), 0.5 mu kidney bean on the plot that's been in cabbage too many years — the beans rest the soil — and 0.5 mu spinach as a quick winter-spring filler before the spring cabbage transplants go out.

Last year's spring cabbage got hit by a late cold snap in April, so I'm holding my transplants back about a week this time. Fall cabbage is where the money is — I target 5,500 kg/mu, and I split the nitrogen: base fertilizer with compost and compound NPK, then two topdressings at rosette and head-forming. That's how I've done it since the soil test three years ago showed my P was already high. I cut back on phosphorus accordingly — no point wasting money.

Maize in summer is almost automatic. After spring cabbage comes off in early June, I rotary-till and plant within 5-7 days. I use a hybrid (Zhengdan 958 type), about 18 kg N/mu split base and jointing-stage topdress. Yield around 500 kg/mu is realistic — I'm not chasing 600.

Irrigation: I have well access but pumping electricity is not cheap. Cabbage needs water — I'll irrigate both cabbage crops 4-5 times each. Maize only if July-August rains fail. Chili needs steady moisture, maybe 5-6 times drip-style from a hose.

Labor is fine — 6 in the household, and I have two adult sons who help with cabbage harvest when the trucks come. I don't hire except for maize harvest if schedules clash.
